$comment: Trailing spoken instructions (#298), schema v1. A delimiter phrase
spoken near the END of a finalized take splits it: everything after
the delimiter is the instruction (it travels as the transform
request's instruction, never as input text), everything before it is
the payload. This table is the configuration: canonical is the
spelling shown in the UI, match_tokens are the whole-token cores a
recognizer may produce (ASR spelling variants included; matching is
case-insensitive and ignores punctuation ,.;:!? attached to the
token), window_words is how many words from the end of a finalized
take the delimiter may sit in.
Closed rules (nothing beyond them is interpreted): the delimiter
matches only within the last window_words words of a FINALIZED take;
among matching occurrences the LAST one wins, earlier ones stay
payload text; a delimiter followed only by whitespace or punctuation
is not an occurrence (no instruction, payload untouched); a
delimiter whose previous token is the language's literal word
(spoken-commands.json) is dictated text, not a delimiter; a quoted
mention never matches, because the opening quote stays attached to
the token and the whole-token core no longer equals a delimiter
token; offsets are Unicode code points. The command region a take's
draft carries spans the delimiter and the instruction; the transform
request strips the leading delimiter token so the model sees only
the instruction.
Semantics: tests/spoken_instructions.py; fixtures/spoken-instructions.json;
Rust port: apps/desktop-gpui/crates/processing/src/instructions.rs.
